title: Modules & Module Patterns
summary: How to structure code into reusable ModuleScripts: namespace tables, singletons, factories, and the conventions that keep large Roblox codebases sane.

details.heading: What a module can return
details.body: Anything: a table of functions (most common), a single function, a value, a class-like constructor, or an object with private state via closures.

explanation.whatItIs: The craft of splitting your game's code into focused ModuleScripts — each owning one job — and wiring them together with require().
explanation.whyItExists: A 3,000-line Script is undebuggable. Modules give you files-with-jobs: InventoryManager, RoundTimer, CoinSpawner — each independently readable and testable.
whenToUse: Namespace pattern: `local M = {}` + functions + `return M` — for utility collections
Singleton pattern: module returns a state table or object — one shared instance per runtime
Factory pattern: module returns a constructor `M.new(...)` that creates fresh objects
Service wrappers: one module per Roblox service isolating all calls to it
whenNotToUse: Don't make a module for three lines used once
Avoid modules that require each other in circles — flatten the dependency direction
explanation.mentalModel:
```text
ReplicatedStorage/
  Modules/
    CoinUtils        (namespace of coin helpers)
    GameState        (singleton store)
    PetFactory       (returns .new())

Script/LocalScript:
  local X = require(path)   -- pull in just what you need
```
Think LEGO: each module is a brick with a clear interface.
tips: One module = one responsibility; name it after that responsibility
Put shared modules in ReplicatedStorage, server-only in ServerStorage/ServerScriptService
Keep module dependencies pointing one direction (high-level → low-level), never circular
Initialize lazily inside an `Init()` function when order matters, rather than in module body
commonMistakes: Modules that do heavy work at require-time, slowing every requirer's startup
Treating a singleton module's state as automatically synced — client and server have separate copies
